question: what window of OSMCha review is dense and diverse enough to train on?
method: count queries (page_size=1) per year; reviewer concentration from a 300-row sample per year

corpus_a_overlap.note: an overlapping id would carry both a revert-derived and a human label, which is the cheapest available cross-source agreement signal

threshold_policy: NOT pre-registered. Per decision 4 in docs/DATA_FOUNDATION.md the exclusion rule is chosen after inspecting this distribution, and the paper states that it was set post-hoc. Per-year numbers are published so a reader can apply a different threshold.

decision.reason: The full available range. Pre-2023 is empty at source, so the lower bound is not a choice. No year is excluded: the most concentrated year has one reviewer at 24% and a top-5 at 52.5%, which is influence, not capture.
decision.disclosure: Per-year concentration is published above so a reader can apply a stricter cut. Concentration rises toward the present, so restricting to recent data would have INCREASED reviewer dominance - the opposite of the naive instinct to prefer the newest slice.
decision.corpus_N_selection: 20,000 random unreviewed changesets from the same window

pre_2023_verified_empty.conclusion: OSMCha queryable review history begins 2023-01. Sharp boundary, verified with narrow-window count queries, not an API artifact.

sampling_correction: The first reviewer-concentration pass walked date windows chronologically and broke after N rows, so with dense data it never left January and its numbers described one month, not a year. Re-sampled across Feb/May/Aug/Nov. The correction mattered: 2024 went from 51% top-5 (worst-looking year) to 36.5% (the most diverse). Both sets of numbers are kept so the error is visible.
